newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria needs 77 bln levs for autumn sowing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria needs 77 bln levs for autumn sowing - paper.

text.p: Bulgaria will need some 77 billion levs ($339.8 million) this autumn to sow 1.2 million hectares of wheat and 300,000 hectares of barley, newspapers said on Thursday.

Quoting remarks by farm minister Krastyo Trendafilov before parliament's agriculture commission, the papers also reiterated that Bulgaria would have to import around 500,000 tonnes of wheat to meet its needs.
"No more than 700,000 tonnes of wheat will be bought on the domestic market this year," the Standart daily quoted Trendafilov as saying.
Bulgaria needs 1.6 million tonnes of grain annually for human consumption alone.
Agriculture ministry officials declined immediate comment on the news reports.

On Wednesday Trendafilov told Reuters he expected the European Commission on September 17 to approve the delivery of some 150,000 tonnes of wheat for Bulgaria on preferential conditions following a recent visit to Sofia by EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler.
Bulgaria also expects to import around 100,000 tonnes of grain worth $25 million under the U.S. Export Credit Guarantee Programme (GSM-102).
Bulgaria has been suffering an acute grain shortage following excessive exports last year and this has been compounded by a poor harvest this summer due to adverse weather and a lack of funds.
